ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart friend who can solve complex math problems, but they can't explain how they do it. That's kinda like what's happening with these big neural networks. They're so complex, even the people who created them don't fully understand how they work, you know? (Kono wa, nan desu ka?)

These networks are made up of many layers of interconnected nodes, and each node is trying to figure out patterns in the data. It's like a big team of tiny experts working together, but they don't really know how they're communicating with each other, (Kore wa, nan no koto desu ka?)

It's hard to explain, but basically, these networks are so good at solving problems that they can learn and adapt on their own, without needing to be explicitly programmed. (Kono wa, nan no koto desu ka?)

But, just like your smart friend, the creators of these networks don't fully understand how they work, and that's what makes them so powerful, (Kono wa, nan desu ka?)

They can do things like recognize images, understand language, and even generate new content, but the "how" behind it is still a mystery, (Kono wa, nan no koto desu ka?)

It's like they're speaking a language that's too complex for humans to understand, (Kore wa, nan no koto desu ka?)

So, even though we can use these networks to do amazing things, we still don't fully understand how they work, (Kono wa, nan desu ka?)

And that's what makes them so fascinating, (Kore wa, nan no koto desu ka?)

I hope that helps! (Arigatou gozaimasu!)
